passages.t: Words like arrows, and ‘God will shoot them with arrows’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David” (verse 1). The prayer begins, “Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy” (verse 1).

The enemies fight with words. They “sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows, ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear” (verses 3 and 4). They plot in secret and say, “Who will see them?” (verse 5). They boast, “We have perfected a secret plan” (verse 6).

Then the psalm turns on one word. “But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded” (verse 7). Their own tongues trip them up (verse 8). People see it and think about what God has done (verse 9). The psalm ends, “Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him” (verse 10).
passages.hearers:
The main picture is archery. A bowman could shoot from cover without being seen. Gossip and slander work the same way. They wound from hiding, and the one who is hit may never know who did it.

In a small town or a king's court, a whispered accusation could ruin a person. The psalm names no one, and so anyone who has been lied about can pray it. The book page has more on prayers from the falsely accused.

Notice the mirror. The wicked shoot ‘suddenly’ (verse 4). God shoots ‘suddenly’ (verse 7). Their arrows were words. Their own words bring them down. The trap they set catches them.

Verse 6 ends with a sigh: “For the inner man and the heart are mysterious” (verse 6). People can hide what they plan. Yet the next verse shows that nothing in the heart is hidden from God.

Shaking the head (verse 8) was a sign of scorn or shock at someone's fall.
passages.later:
Proverbs puts it simply: “He who digs a pit will fall into it” (Proverbs 26:27).

James writes of the tongue, “no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison” (James 3:8). And Jesus said secrets do not stay secret: “What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight” (Luke 12:3).
passages.asks:
If you have been hurt by gossip or lies, this psalm is for you. It lets you tell God how sharp the words were. It also promises that hidden plans are not hidden from him. You do not have to fire back.

And it asks a harder question. Have your own words ever been arrows? ‘Who will see them?’ is the thought behind most gossip. God sees.
